coverage.found: Market butchers must show the slaughter-inspection stamp and keep slaughter certificates on delivery. No stall-level reporting or software gap found. Nothing new. Poultry-slaughter registration not found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Beekeepers file a 'beekeeping fact declaration' at the township office (COA/Agriculture and Food Agency procedure, 2024 leaflet). Miaoli DARES provides a free 'bee calendar' record and traceability system. Free public tool, small niche. See candidate C05 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Animal-drug sellers must keep a resident qualified manager with training renewed every 2 years and file closure within 30 days. Pharmacies and vets must keep purchase proof for human drugs used on pets for 3 years (paper or electronic). No Taiwan e-reporting of antimicrobial use found. See candidate C09 (weak).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Well-drilling firms (Groundwater Drilling Business Rules, amended 2015): 5-year licence renewable 60-30 days before expiry, completion report data within 30 days, 30-day filings for staff or ownership changes, 6-hour training every 5 years logged in the authority's management system. Existing wells: city 'well declaration and registration' systems (Taichung has an app). See candidates C04 and C05b.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Septic and night-soil haulers need a clearance permit covering waste code D-0104 under the Waste Disposal Act; unlisted vehicles face criminal penalties; Taichung illegal-dumping incident in 2025 raised enforcement. Whether a manifest is required for night soil is unconfirmed. See candidate C06.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lift managers (owners or management committees) must apply for an annual safety inspection before the permit expires (30 days or 2 months, sources differ) and keep monthly maintenance records. Maintenance firms need insurance and at least 6 technicians for up to 200 lifts. The Control Yuan found the Ministry of the Interior lacked data on lift numbers and inspection status. No reminder app found. Boilers and pressure vessels not reached. See candidate C02.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Simple water supply systems (簡易自來水) are governed by local regulations under the Water Supply Act and maintained by the operators themselves. Local governments run annual survey and sampling programmes. Filing frequency not found. See candidate C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K12 (rejected: the regulator supplies the software). Not re-searched. Fertiliser dealers not checked.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K09 (rejected). Not re-searched.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Pre-need funeral contracts require a firm with at least NT$30M paid-in capital and 3 years of operation, which excludes small operators. Taipei revised its penalty table effective 2026-02-01. Results from mainland China's 2026 funeral regulations are not Taiwan law. Nothing new for small firms.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations must file an annual work plan and budget before the year starts, a report and accounts within 2-3 months of year end (Taipei: by end of March), and re-elect directors on time (terms up to 4 years). No association-management software found. Halal certification is run by the Chinese Muslim Association and the Taiwan Muslim Association; no fee or software data found. See candidate C03.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi operators must report hiring and dismissal of drivers to the police unit that issued the driver's registration card (Motor Vehicle Transportation Business Regulations, version dated 2026-05-06 on the search result). Annual vehicle inspection rules not found. See candidate C11.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers (外幣收兌處): quarterly report to Bank of Taiwan by the 15th of the month after quarter end, cap raised-risk limit of USD 3,000 per person per transaction (2021 amendment), books kept 10 years and exchange slips 5 years, AML procedures. Vendor-side duties not searched. See candidate C12.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childminders and nurseries: subsidy contracts submitted to the home-childcare service centre within 7 days, annual claims by 20 December (Taichung), nursery accreditation cycles; at least four daily-record apps already exist (Skybaby, KIDSDAY, 愛托付, 開蒙). Driving schools: MOTC proposed tighter rules for 2026 (retraining after licence revocation), final status unconfirmed. Tattoo studios, hunting outfitters and small food producers not reached; K01 covers food traceability.

coverage.category: 37. Vehicle repair shops and motorcycle shops (waste oil, tyre records); also row 'Vehicle repair, motorcycle shops and used-car dealers (waste oil, waste batteries/tyres, ELV records)'
coverage.found: Taiwan duty now partly verified. Waste lubricant oil: per New Taipei EPB guidance (rule effective 2012-01-01 under EPA household-waste classification), motorcycle shops/garages/petrol stations act as household waste-oil collection points; their own waste oil must go to a licensed hauler/processor, and they must keep hauler/processor name, date and quantity records for 3 years for audit (local-level source; other counties unverified). No evidence found that small repair shops must file online waste declarations: I could not confirm whether 汽車修理業 is in the MOENV online-declaration designated list (the list is threshold-based). Waste batteries/tyres go through the responsible-manufacturer recycling-fund system (fee paid by makers/importers), not by the shop. No dedicated Taiwan-language workshop software found (search returned only foreign products: Tallermatic, MotorWorks, Workshop Software), but that was one English-skewed search, so competition is unverified. Possible real bridge: private motorcycle emissions-inspection stations (機車排氣定檢站, Air Pollution Control Act Art. 18 / 檢驗站設置及管理辦法, amended 2019-07-03) are mostly motorcycle shops with required certificates, trained inspectors and camera monitoring; paper reminders are being replaced by SMS (New Taipei from 2026-01-01); late-inspection fines are NT$500 then NT$3,000. Online upload format, software requirement and station count were not verified. Nothing new beyond a weak/unverified lead.

No 2025-2026 notice extending traceability to restaurants was found. The registration is free and run by the state; annual reconfirmation is a thin software hook. Restaurant tier of traceability: nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.found: Online business-waste declaration (Waste Disposal Act Art. 31) applies only to designated businesses by threshold (tonnage / hazardous kg / sector), listing expanded over years (about 38,000 firms around 2013); I could not confirm that small shops are listed. Responsible-party recycling-fund duty: manufacturers/importers of listed recyclables declare operating or import volumes online on odd months (30th) via the 應回收廢棄物責任業者管理辦法; this falls on makers/importers/chains, not micro shops. Single-use tableware restrictions (amended 2023-08-01) and beverage-cup rules (chain drink shops, convenience stores, fast food, supermarkets: NT$5 discount for own cup since 2022-07-01, plastic single-use cups phased out from September 2024 or 2025 with local timetables; breakfast shops and night markets outside scope) are in-store compliance rules with no filing; at most a signage / discount-tracking need. No filing bridge found. Nothing new beyond K02 / K05.

Chinese-medicine shops must have a resident qualified person. A June 2026 Chiayi case shows investigators checking forged sales documents used to obtain the business-proof certificate. Count of shops not found. Record-keeping years and licence renewal cycle unverified. Small one-off qualification/registration wave with a possible compliance-paperwork angle, but the rule's stability is contested.

coverage.category: Business-tax and e-invoice duties for micro-businesses (小規模營業人 查定課徵, e-invoice rollout)
coverage.found: Strongest finding. Ministry of Finance rule (announced March 2026): 大眾化消費飲食店 (soy-milk shops, ice shops, noodle shops, buffet, bento) previously exempt from uniform invoices at 1% assessed tax will stop being 'specially operated' businesses from 2029-01-01 (ROC 118); shops with average monthly sales at or above NT$200,000 must then issue uniform invoices at 5%. A 3-year buffer (2026-01-01 to 2028-12-31) lets approved shops keep 1% and no invoices if they adopt mobile payment or KIOSK checkout; application deadline reported as 2028-06-30; stop conditions reported as mobile-payment share of assessed sales at zero or below a target (e.g. under 5% cumulative over 4 quarters) or quarterly sales reaching NT$2.4m. Affected counts conflict: about 5,300 shops at NT$200k+ per MOF versus about 70,000 on the 1% assessed regime per officials; 11,684 shops still on the concession at end-2025 (9,281 restaurants). Chain or franchise stores must use uniform invoices. KIOSK vendors can file the concession application for shops. MOF says the 2029 date may be adjusted ('rolling'). Separately, e-invoice upload duty (Business Tax Act Art. 32-1): upload within 7 days for business buyers and 2 days for non-business; fines NT$1,500-15,000 since 2025-07-01. No 2026-2027 expansion of B2B e-invoice mandates was found. Candidate created.

result.competitor: I found no Taiwanese jewellery POS or ERP product with an AML module. Searches in Chinese for 銀樓 POS/系統/軟體 and 洗錢防制 returned only foreign jewellery ERPs (GoldMatrix, NB Jewel, Aurum, BUSY, Odoo/ERPNext add-ons) and none of them is built for Taiwan's AML rules. The free alternatives are MOEA's Q&A, its quick guide, its internal control and risk assessment template (114.4 edition) and paper reporting forms. Whether the MJIB has an online reporting portal was not reached. Whether local POS vendors bundle AML features was not reached.
result.duty: The duty is confirmed in the MOEA rule 銀樓業防制洗錢與打擊資恐辦法, last amended 114.04.24 (2025-04-24). It covers any company or firm that sells precious metals, gems or jewellery wholesale or retail, whether or not it belongs to the trade association. Rules: ID check (CDD) for cash deals of NT$500k or more. Cash-transaction report to the MJIB within 5 business days, on a stamped form sent by mail, fax or email. Suspicious-transaction report within 10 business days; urgent cases go by fax first. Sanctions-list match report within 10 business days. Enhanced checks (EDD) for PEPs and high-risk customers. Records kept in original form for 5 years. Risk assessment report updated every 2 years. Internal control and audit system. Owner or designated officer trained every 2 years, plus training for new staff. MOEA inspects each year, on site or off site. Penalty under the Money Laundering Control Act for designated non-financial businesses: NT$50k to 1M per a Taipei City government deck. A 2026 news item on accounting firms cites NT$50k to 5M, so the current upper limit is unconfirmed. I found no enforcement cases against jewellery shops.
result.market: No official count of jewellery shops was found. An older 理財周刊 article estimates over 4,000 jewellery shops in Taiwan, from a survey around 2005. A current figure would need business-register data by industry code or the national jewellery association's membership list; neither was reached.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Taiwan's 銀樓業防制洗錢與打擊資恐辦法 (last amended 2025-04-24) requires ID checks and a report to the Investigation Bureau within 5 business days for cash deals of NT$500k or more. Suspicious deals must be reported within 10 business days. Shops must keep records for 5 years, update a risk assessment every 2 years, and train staff every 2 years. MOEA inspects every year. Fines are about NT$50k to 1M, though the current upper limit is unconfirmed. I found no Taiwanese jewellery POS or AML product, but MOEA gives out free templates and paper forms. Most small shops rarely see NT$500k cash deals, and the heavier tasks come only every two years. That means low frequency and low willingness to pay. The likely channel is the trade association or an add-on module sold by POS vendors.

result.competitor: State system: NLMA documents (2020) say firms and inspectors must upload photos of completion and safety inspections and of each monthly maintenance record form, with the lift's unique code, to a national system (Taipei calls it the 昇降設備/機械停車設備使用許可證全國連線交換系統). That partly covers record-keeping. In practice, maintenance firms often apply for the inspection on the owner's behalf. The Shinyi 社區幫 app covers community notices but not lift tracking. Foreign field-service tools (SmartService, FieldBoss, Shifton, Planfix) cover the vendor side, but none found is localised for Taiwan. No Taiwan-specific commercial reminder or tracker was found.
result.duty: Building Act Art. 77-4 (cited via secondary sources): a lift needs a use permit, and the manager must have a registered professional firm maintain it every month. Regulation (建築物昇降設備設置及檢查管理辦法; latest version seen dated 2020-06-12 via a Changhua copy that returned 503): yearly safety inspection, with the permit issued by the inspection body. Application window: 'within 30 days before the permit expires' per NLMA documents; 'within 2 months' per the Taichung lift manager's guide and the NCUT procedure. This conflict is unresolved because the law.moj text was not reached. Monthly maintenance record in two copies, signed by the manager and the technician. Penalty: a lift that fails is not allowed to operate and the permit can be revoked after spot checks. The fine amount for not applying was not verified.
result.market: I found no national lift count. Control Yuan figure (c. 2014): Taipei alone had 31,587 lifts, and at least 13,000 nationally missed inspection deadlines. The MOI dataset 14376 lists the number of professional firms, technicians and inspection bodies, but no values were visible; the link points to ROC year 109. National lifts plausibly number 100k or more and registered firms a few hundred, but both are unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Building Act Art. 77-4 and the lift regulation require monthly maintenance by a registered firm and a yearly safety inspection to renew the use permit. Sources disagree on the window: national documents say apply within 30 days before expiry, Taichung and school documents say within 2 months. I found no Taiwan tracker for management committees. Pain is low, though. Maintenance firms usually file the inspection for owners, and the state upload system already holds photos of monthly records. Volunteer committees are hard to sell to and unlikely to pay. Lift firms would compare a vendor edition against field-service software. The regulation text and penalty amount were not read directly.

result.competitor: The core reporting job is already covered for free by the state soilmove e-manifest system and app, and some cities run their own (Taichung's app, Tainan's QR-code checks at yards). NLMA-approved GPS vendors sell boxes bundled with their own fleet platforms, offering live tracking and trip history. One vendor (a LINE official page) claims a single unit meets both NLMA and MOENV specs. Neither the state system nor the GPS vendors appear to link dispatch, manifests and cost or disposal-fee ledgers in a SaaS for small haulers, but I did not reach that conclusion exhaustively. Foreign analogues exist (SoilFLO, Soil Connect eRegulatory) but they are not localized for Taiwan. I could not confirm whether the state system offers an API or data export, so integration risk is high.
result.duty: Real and in force. Since 1 Jan 2026 the NLMA's (國土管理署) nationwide full-flow regime for construction surplus soil (營建剩餘土石方) applies. Every trip from site to receiving yard needs an electronic manifest (電子聯單) showing the project, route, soil type and volume, and every truck must carry a GPS unit that has passed NLMA type approval. The type-approval procedure is published on nlma.gov.tw. The NLMA gave a GPS transition buffer to the end of February 2026 and opened GPS applications to small trucks. The frequency is every trip. Penalties are not uniform yet: enforcement currently runs through the administrative scheme and local rules, and I did not find a specific national fine. The draft Waste Disposal Act Article 10-1 (MOENV notice of 29 May 2025) would make online reporting and GPS mandatory and let MOI set national rules and penalties. UDN reported on 18 May 2026 that the bill was only in Legislative Yuan committee review. One summary mentions a third reading, but I could not date it or confirm that the soil clause survived. Treat the amendment as pending or unverified.
result.market: About 15,000 gravel and soil trucks nationwide (UDN and CTEE, Jan-Feb 2026). One undated report gives 6,743 NLMA GPS applications, of which 6,223 were cleared to operate, plus 1,649 MOENV-equipped trucks. There are about 140 soil storage and processing yards (土資場), but only 18 operating sites with fill capacity (Dec 2025). I found no register count of hauling firms; a guess of a few thousand mostly small owner-operator firms is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real, applies to every trip, and caused a national crisis in early 2026 (the "土方之亂"). But the state e-manifest system is free, and GPS vendors already bundle fleet tracking, so the remaining gap is only the dispatch and ledger layer that ties manifests to fees and costs. Small haulers are fragmented owner-operators who are not very digital and are price-sensitive (GPS units sell for around NT$380). Whether the state system has an API is unknown, which makes the MVP risky. The pending Waste Disposal Act changes may alter the rules again. GPS vendors and industry associations are the natural channels, but those vendors could add this feature themselves. The opportunity is moderate to low for a solo founder.

MOI inspects each year, on site or remotely.

Per the Kaohsiung National Taxation Bureau, as relayed by the 104 blog and Commonwealth Magazine (GVM): the shop cannot apply itself and must authorise every mobile-payment provider it uses to apply for it, and those providers send the shop's sales data straight to the tax office. The tax office therefore calculates the mobile-payment share from provider data, and KIOSK makers can apply for the shop. That leaves only a nice-to-have dashboard. Whether iCHEF or other POS systems show the share was not confirmed, but payment providers' merchant back-ends already show mobile-payment totals. The 2029 switch to e-invoices is covered by many existing POS and e-invoice vendors and by MOF's free e-invoice platform.
result.duty: Real and in force. In December 2025 the Ministry of Finance (MOF) amended and renamed the guideline to 查定課徵營業人使用行動支付及多媒體資訊服務機適用租稅優惠作業規範. Small businesses taxed on assessed sales that take mobile payments or use a KIOSK with mobile-payment checkout keep the 1% assessed rate and stay exempt from uniform invoices until 2028-12-31, even above NT$200k a month. Applications close 2028-06-30. The concession stops in any of three cases: a quarter's mobile-payment share of assessed sales is zero; the cumulative share misses its target; or a quarter's sales reach NT$2.4m. Press reports give the cumulative targets as 5% for quarters 1-4, then 9%, 13%, 17% and 21% for later two-quarter periods. Their layout is garbled, and I did not confirm these figures from the official text. From 2029-01-01, mass-market eateries (大眾化飲食店) with assessed monthly sales of NT$200k or more must issue uniform invoices (reported by CTEE in March 2026). The penalty is losing the concession: the shop moves to the 5% general regime and must issue invoices. The condition is checked quarterly. I found no reports that the 2029 date has changed.

result.reason: The duty is real and checked every quarter, but the core job is not the shop's. I found no dedicated software, but the core job is already covered by the EPA WCDS portal, GPS vendors and local-bureau reporting. The NT$2m fine (effective April 2025) applies to illegal operators, not to late reporting. Legal homestays number 12,551 and illegal ones 566 (2025 Tourism Administration figures). Duty is real: Factory Management and Counselling Act (2019 amendment) requires managed unregistered low-pollution factories to pay an annual counselling fee, with a 30-day cure period before the application is rejected. Penalties include power and water cut-off and demolition. Filing an improvement plan by 19 Mar 2023 and holding a special factory registration by 19 Mar 2030 (longest extension) are the milestones. Market: about 27,148 factories were in managed status as of Nov 2024, and 9,688 held registration. About 17,000 remain in process. Competition: no dedicated software found, but I could not check this thoroughly. Likely consultants and architects do the work. Weaknesses: the work is mostly one-off and site-specific (land, building, pollution improvements), the annual fee is a simple payment to local government, and the 2030 deadline is a single event. No 2026 extension or count was found.
